questions.q: When a journal posts in Oracle Fusion General Ledger, what happens to the account's balance?
options: Nothing, balances must be recalculated manually from journal lines
A summarized balance for that account combination, period, and balance type is updated automatically
The balance is only updated once a quarter
Balances are stored only in the subledger, never in General Ledger
questions.explain: Posting updates a maintained summarized balance in addition to storing the detail journal line, so a balance can be looked up instantly.

questions.q: What is the purpose of the Inquire on Detail Balances page?
options: To look up an account's balance directly, without running a formal report
To define a new chart of accounts segment
questions.explain: Inquire on Detail Balances lets you enter a ledger, period, and account combination and get the balance back immediately, with drill-down options.

questions.q: For a balance sheet account like Cash, which time frame is normally used to read the balance?
options: Year-to-date (life-to-date), since the balance does not reset each period
It cannot be inquired on at all
questions.explain: Balance sheet accounts carry forward; they are read year-to-date (effectively life-to-date) rather than resetting each period like expenses.

questions.q: A reviewer wants to know what Utilities Expense cost specifically in the month of March. Which time frame should they select?
questions.explain: Period-to-date (PTD) isolates activity recorded in that single period, which is what "what did March cost" requires.

questions.q: What is typically the next step after an account inquiry reveals an unexpected balance?
options: Drill from the summarized balance into the journal lines (and potentially subledger transactions) behind it
questions.explain: An inquiry is the starting point for investigation; drilling into the underlying journal lines (and subledger detail) is how the cause gets identified.
